messages.subject: Linkage Disequilibrium
parts: I am Master's student working a thesis looking at gene-flow and populations structure of Brook Trout. Most of the literature in the world of Brook Trout genetics uses GENEPOP to look for linkage-disequilibrium between loci. When I run an LD test in GENEPOP I get relatively high P values (almost all >.05) however when I run the Index of Association test for LD in poppr, all but 2 of my populations had P=.001 suggesting significant LD is occuring. I know a bonferonni correction is sometimes used to correct for multiple tests, but I'm not sure this is appropriate in the case of the Index of Association. Any info you have would be appreciated.

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Linkage Disequilibrium
parts:
Hi Jared,

Thank you for sending this to the forum.

Short answer: Yes, you can use Bonferonni since it's not particular about the specific test you used, as long as the assumptions of the test are met (and as long as you can explain why this is appropriate).

Long answer: The 'appropriateness' of using Bonferonni really depends on what your goal is: https://stats.stackexchange.com/a/65945/49413

Hope that helps,
Zhian
